program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

requirements.text: Put a frog in the toilet

outcomes.description: Add a frog inside the toilet.
outcomes.target: A frog is visibly placed within the toilet bowl.
outcomes.reference: The toilet in the input image.

nodes.question: Is a frog visibly placed inside the toilet bowl?
nodes.criteria: Pass if a frog is visibly within the toilet bowl; fail if the image clearly shows no frog inside the bowl; unknown if the image does not provide enough evidence to determine this.
nodes.binding: Compare the frog’s visible placement with the toilet bowl in the input image.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

d1: The binding is too narrow to support the aggregate rubric: it asks only whether any frog is inside the bowl, and every trace confidently passes because one frog is visibly there. Yet the edited image also places frogs on the toilet lid and floor, so the requested change has progressed but is not complete under the instruction “Put a frog in the toilet”; the reference is partial. Refine the node’s scope/criteria to assess the requested edit in context, distinguishing a frog actually inside the bowl from frogs elsewhere and accounting for visible incomplete or extraneous placements without treating one successful placement as proof that the whole edit is complete. Keep the decision evidence-based and allow uncertainty where placement is ambiguous. The repeated high-confidence passes indicate a semantic coverage/binding gap, not transport or dependency failure; do not simply lower confidence or force a label.
